titleText.es: Ustedes me toman por loco. Pero los locos no saben nada. ¿Podría un loco haber burlado a los mejores artistas de electrónica/techno de nuestra era? Lo próximo en caer será el grupo de house/trance de Roderick Usher.
titleText.en: You fancy me mad. Could a madman have outsmarted the greatest electronica/techno artists of our era? Next to fall will be Roderick Usher's house/trance band.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive preserves this translated raster under an erroneous original link to xkcd #739 and a 2010-05-12 manifest date; its filename, panel art, dialogue, and title text correspond to official xkcd #740, The Tell-Tale Beat, dated 2010-05-14. The Spanish title text adds ‘Pero los locos no saben nada.’ to the Poe quotation; the English text here preserves the official #740 title attribute exactly.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Maté is the speaker form of matar for one completed action in the past. The written accent on the final é is required for this past form.
Escondí is the speaker form of esconder for one completed action in the past. The ending -í identifies the speaker and carries a written accent.

example.es: Escondí la llave en un cajón.
example.en: I hid the key in a drawer.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cuerpos is the plural of cuerpo, “body.” In a context involving death, it can refer specifically to dead bodies or corpses.
Persiguen is a present form of perseguir for several doers. It can describe a physical chase, or figuratively describe memories, sounds, or worries that keep troubling someone.
Latidos is the plural of latido. It most often names the beats of a heart, but it can also describe repeated throbs or pulses.

example.es: Oigo los latidos de mi corazón.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: El ritmo delator · Daft Punk · UNN-TSS
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do Poe's story and Daft Punk turn the pounding noise into the comic's joke?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The murderer from Poe's The Tell-Tale Heart has killed the electronic duo Daft Punk, so the guilty heartbeat becomes an electronic dance beat.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In Edgar Allan Poe's story, a murderer hides a body beneath the floorboards, becomes convinced that he hears the victim's heart beating, and reveals his guilt. The comic replaces the victim with Daft Punk and writes the pounding as UNN-TSS, an imitation of a dance-music beat. The Spanish title changes “heart” to ritmo, “rhythm.” The title text adds another Poe reference through Roderick Usher, while house and trance are electronic-music genres and house also echoes The Fall of the House of Usher.

applications.explanationEn: Desde que introduces the starting event, maté supplies its completed-past verb, and a los marks the specific people involved in that event.
A appears before the article los because Daft Punk names specific people who directly receive the action.
Maté presents the killing as one bounded, completed event in the past.

Escondí presents the hiding as one bounded, completed event in the past.
